book.title: Seduced by Story: The Use and Abuse of Narrative

argument.statement: Narrative’s “dangerously alluring” power enables deception, so contemporary fashion in story—used as excuse or explanation—should be questioned rather than embraced uncritically.

book.rationale: The book critically examines the role of narrative in various contexts, placing it primarily within the realm of literary and cultural criticism.
book.summary: In this spiritual sequel to his influential Reading for the Plot, Peter Brooks examines the dangerously alluring power of storytelling. “There’s nothing in the world more powerful than a good story. Nothing can stop it. Nothing can defeat it.” So begins the scholar and literary critic Peter Brooks’s reckoning with today’s flourishing cult of story. Forty years after publishing his seminal work Reading for the Plot, his important contribution to what came to be known as the “narrative turn” in contemporary criticism and philosophy, Brooks returns to question the unquestioning fashion in which story is now embraced as an excuse or explanation and the fact that every brand or politician comes equipped with one. In a discussion that ranges from The Girl on the Train to legal argument, Brooks reminds us that among the powers of narrative is the power to deceive.
